discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 261803
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
103 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A steady rain and gusty winds continue this afternoon through
  Friday, though winds and rain intensity diminish with time
  later tonight into Friday. 

- Wet snow may mix in at times later tonight into Friday
  morning. Light slushy accumulations possible in spots, though
  roads should remain wet.

- Another round of rain Sunday into Sunday evening. 

- Mainly dry with gradual warming next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 103 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

A large eastern CONUS low pressure system, double-barreled with one 
center lifting up the east coast and another taking a northeast 
track just west of the Appalachians, will continue to provide the 
local area with blustery/cool conditions and a steady rain for the 
remainder of today through at least Friday morning. Aggressive 
moisture surge and isentropic ascent within a 50-65 kt easterly jet 
in the 850-700 mb layer brings more moderate rainfall this afternoon 
and evening. Deformation forcing lingering on the western flank of 
the system by later tonight and Friday with rainfall intensity and 
coverage likely waning a bit with time, especially by later Friday 
morning and afternoon when some dry pockets emerge. Modest CAA on 
the backside of the low cold make it possible for wet snow to mix in 
later tonight into Friday morning in spots. Still not expecting much 
in the way of impacts given the wet ground and sfc temps/dewpoints 
holding in the mid-upper 30s. The primary impacts from this system 
still appear to be the widespread 1" or so rainfall totals, and 
gusty northeast winds this afternoon-evening in the 30-40 mph range. 

Saturday will feature weak warm advection and some sunshine as the 
large low pressure system exits east and a trailing small scale 
perturbation bypasses north of the area. A deeper, more progressive 
shortwave trough remains on target to track east through the OH 
Valley and Great Lakes Sunday into Sunday evening. Ensemble and 
deterministic model solutions now generally agree on an associated 
sfc low track through the OH Valley. Forcing and moisture return 
will bring another round of primarily rain with amounts up to near a 
half inch possible. Much of next week then appears mainly dry with 
gradual moderation thanks to a transition to a lower amplitude, 
split flow regime. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1151 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

A soggy and breezy Thanksgiving is on tap for today. Widespread
rainfall can be seen on radar overspreading the area from the 
southeast as of midday as a large area of low pressure moves up 
the East Coast. Light to moderate rain will continue this 
afternoon with MVFR ceilings and visibilities. Heavier pockets 
of rain will likely develop this evening with potential for IFR
visibilities, although confidence is low on exactly where and 
when that occurs. Ceilings will drop to IFR after sunset and 
continue through Friday morning. Winds remain strong today out 
of the northeast as a tightening pressure gradient sets up over 
the area. Winds will be sustained around 15 to 20 kts this 
afternoon and evening with gusts as high as 30 to 35 kts 
(primarily at KFWA and east). Winds will diminish a bit after 
sunset but remain breezy with gusts of 20 to 25 kts overnight 
into Friday morning. Rain continues through Friday morning, with
potential for some wet snow to mix in at times. No snow 
accumulation is expected. Rain tapers off from west to east 
Friday afternoon.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM EST this afternoon for LMZ043-
     046.
     Gale Warning until 1 AM EST Friday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 261620

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1020 AM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

   Valid 261630Z - 271200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   FAR EASTERN NORTH CAROLINA INTO SOUTHEAST VIRGINIA...AND COASTAL
   WASHINGTON...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms capable of isolated severe gusts and perhaps a brief
   tornado remain possible today from parts of far eastern North
   Carolina into southeast Virginia, and also coastal Washington.

   ...Far Eastern North Carolina into Southeast Virginia...
   As of late morning, water-vapor satellite imagery shows a strong
   mid-level shortwave trough pivoting northward over the Carolinas
   towards the Mid-Atlantic. A broken band of low-topped convection
   producing occasional lightning flashes extends from near the surface
   low over far eastern/coastal NC southward into the shelf waters just
   offshore. The 12z MHX observed sounding preceding this convection
   depicted weak lapse rates aloft and minimal boundary-layer
   instability, but around 650 J/kg MUCAPE with a saturated profile.

   As the surface low develops northward to the Chesapeake Bay vicinity
   by late afternoon, a narrow zone of modest buoyancy may overspread
   the immediate coastal counties from far eastern NC into the southern
   portion of the Chesapeake Bay vicinity. Stronger low-level
   flow/shear will tend to remain north of the effective warm front
   extending east-northeastward from the surface low. Still, occasional
   convectively augmented strong/gusty winds may occur with ongoing
   thunderstorms before they move offshore later this afternoon. A
   brief embedded tornado also remains possible, although expectations
   for very weak instability should limit the overall severe threat
   over land. See Mesoscale Discussion 2469 for more details on the
   near-term severe threat across this region.

   ...Coastal Washington...
   A very strong upper-level jet will extend from the eastern Pacific
   into the Pacific Northwest today. The 12Z UIL observed sounding
   shows a moist boundary layer with weak instability (around 250 J/kg
   MLCAPE). Strong west-southwesterly low-level flow noted in recent
   VWPs from KLGX will aid in substantial 0-3 km speed shear, but flow
   in this layer should veer/gradually weaken through the afternoon.
   Even so, some risk may exist in the short-term for strong,
   low-topped convection to pose a gusty wind/brief tornado threat
   across parts of coastal/northwest WA.

   ..Gleason/Karstens.. 11/26/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 261700

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1100 AM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms appear possible Friday afternoon and evening
   over portions of western Oregon.

   ...Synopsis...

   An intense deep-layer cyclone over the upper OH Valley at 12Z Friday
   will move into New England ahead of a short-wave trough progressing
   from the northern Plains into the Upper Midwest. Elsewhere, a
   low-amplitude short-wave trough will move onto the Pacific Northwest
   coast Friday evening and into portions of the Interior West Friday
   night into early Saturday. Ahead of that disturbance, sufficient air
   mass destabilization may occur to support a few deeper convective
   updrafts capable of lightning from the vicinity of the OR coast
   toward the Cascades. Across the remainder of the CONUS, dry and
   stable conditions will preclude thunderstorm development.

   ..Mead.. 11/26/2026

spc.summary: Widely scattered thunderstorms appear possible late Saturday night from portions of the Ozark Plateau into the Mid-South and lower Mississippi Valley.
spc.text:
SPC AC 261910

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0110 PM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Widely scattered thunderstorms appear possible late Saturday night
   from portions of the Ozark Plateau into the Mid-South and lower
   Mississippi Valley.

   ...Synopsis...

   The progression of an upper-level jet streak from the Interior West
   into the southern Plains will contribute to midlevel trough
   amplification over the central and southern Plains into the Ozark
   Plateau Saturday afternoon into Saturday night. In response, surface
   cyclogenesis will occur over the southern High Plains on Saturday
   with the low subsequently developing into central or southern MO by
   Saturday night. The surface low will be attended by a cold front,
   which is forecast to strengthen while surging southeast through the
   southern Plains and Ozark Plateau.


   ...Ozark Plateau into the Mid-South and lower Mississippi Valley...

   Southerly low-level flow will strengthen ahead of the surface low
   and cold front, allowing a partially modified Gulf air mass (i.e.,
   boundary-layer dewpoints in the 50s to low 60s) to advance inland
   through the Ark-La-Tex toward the Mid-South and lower MS Valley
   Saturday night. That moistening process will occur beneath
   steepening midlevel lapse rates, yielding a poleward-expanding
   corridor of weak instability, characterized by MUCAPE of generally
   less than 500 J/kg. 

   Height falls aloft and warm advection occurring along a nocturnally
   strengthening low-level jet are expected to contribute to at least
   widely scattered thunderstorm development Saturday night into early
   Sunday morning along and ahead of the surface cold front. Both
   low-level and deep-layer shear are forecast to strengthen at that
   time within the warm sector; however, forecast soundings suggest
   storms will likely remain slightly elevated atop a shallow,
   near-ground inversion, which is expected to limit severe weather
   potential.

   ..Mead.. 11/26/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
